what: vfx accepts a frame of up to 2^32 bytes (32768x32768 at 8 bpc, 23170 square at 16, 16384 square at 32). The crate refuses a frame when (w+128)*(h+128) >= (2^31-1)/8, which is 16255 square at 8 and 16 bpc, or when the frame is over 2^31-1 bytes, which is 11585 square at 32 bpc. 16384x16384 is refused at every depth.
evidence: d8.crate_max_square_side,d16.crate_max_square_side,d32.crate_max_square_side,d8.crate_frame_size_16384x16384,vfx.limit_depth8_square_32768_ok,vfx.limit_depth32_16384_ok;src/pixfmt.rs check_dims and the 2 GiB test in plane_layout
suggested_handling: Call PixFmt::frame_size(w, h) before spawning and refuse with the crate's text; never advertise the 4 GiB limit of vfx for the pipeline. 7680x4320 and 15360x8640 pass at all three depths.

what: ffmpeg decodes an untagged 1280x720 or larger source with its own default (BT.601); tools/apply.py names bt709 by the size rule. The crate Decoder has no matrix option, so a plain Decoder (size() only, or nothing) differs from the wrapper: 5084657 of 11059200 bytes at 8 bpc (largest byte difference 41), 11907031 of 22118400 bytes at 16 bpc and 22486921 of 44236800 bytes at 32 bpc.
suggested_handling: Always pass filter("[fps=R,]scale=in_color_matrix=M") with M chosen by the apply.py rule (contract_colour.tsv). A source that carries a colorspace tag decodes identically either way (decode.hd_bt709.*), but the pipeline cannot rely on the tag being present.

what: DecoderBuilder::size appends a second scale=W:H after the user filter; with filter(scale=in_color_matrix=M) the result still differs from the wrapper's decode (5124713 of 11059200 bytes at 8 bpc; 10604208 of 22118400 at 16 bpc), apparently because the second scale does the conversion with ffmpeg's default matrix (not examined further).
suggested_handling: Do not combine filter() with size(). The frame size comes from the plan (displayed size); the dry-run measurement is not needed. If size() is wanted, scale_flags("bicubic:in_color_matrix=M") gave identical bytes (variant B) but is a workaround.

what: Encoder has no -vf slot. Without out_color_matrix and setparams in output_args ffmpeg converts rgba to yuv420p its own way and writes no colour tags (range, space, transfer, primaries all unknown); the luma of a 1280x720 frame differs in 920021 of 921600 samples.
suggested_handling: Pass -vf scale=out_color_matrix=M:out_range=tv,setparams=...:range=tv in output_args (verified: tags and decoded frames equal to apply.py). The lossless path writes RGB with no tags, like apply.py.

what: For a variable rate input apply.py takes avg_frame_rate as the rate and decodes with fps=R. Without it the frame count differs: 62 frames expected, 60 with the crate default (-fps_mode passthrough) and 76 with ffmpeg's own default, for a 60 frame clip with gaps (r_frame_rate 24/1, avg_frame_rate 720/37).
suggested_handling: Implement the apply.py rule exactly: vfr when |avg - r| / r > 1/1000, rate = avg when vfr, else r (fall back to avg). Put fps=N/D first in filter().

what: libx264 output is not byte reproducible. The same encode command, recorded run: 15 runs: 5 distinct files ({'fd68c14e4db0': 11, 'eef770139aeb': 1, '906ec2775790': 1, '7e89ae5af00e': 1, '0c2f0e65133c': 1}), 5 distinct decoded streams with default threads and, with -threads 1, 15 runs: 1 distinct files ({'a832d4bb9511': 15}), 1 distinct decoded streams. A byte comparison of two lossy outputs, from the pipeline and from apply.py, is not a valid test (two runs of apply.py alone already differ).
suggested_handling: Compare pipeline and wrapper through --lossless (ffv1, decoded frames equal) and compare lossy outputs by decoded frames with a tolerance (mean absolute difference of decoded rgba 0.5 or less held in every case here), plus the stream facts (codec, pix_fmt, range, tags).

what: neutral_ffmpeg::probe_file reads only a fixed subset. It has no color_space, color_primaries, color_transfer (so no matrix choice and no HDR refusal), no rotation (side data or rotate tag), no disposition (cover art), no tags, and its width and height are the coded size.
suggested_handling: Run ffprobe with the apply.py arguments (-v quiet -print_format json -show_streams -show_format) through neutral_ffmpeg::exec::run_capture and read the JSON with neutral_ffmpeg::json::Json; or extend the crate (owner decision).

what: Lookup order differs. Crate: explicit option, FFMPEG or FFPROBE, PATH. apply.py: --ffmpeg-path or MEDIA_FFMPEG_PATH, FFMPEG, PATH, then %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Links, %ProgramFiles%\ffmpeg\bin, %ProgramFiles(x86)%\ffmpeg\bin. A machine that works with apply.py through MEDIA_FFMPEG_PATH or a WinGet link only is not found by the crate.
suggested_handling: Resolve both programs in apply.py's order in the pipeline and hand the result to Binaries::with_ffmpeg and with_ffprobe.

what: All four registered effects are temporal. vfx copies all of stdin to a spool file (vfx-spool-<pid>-<nanos>-<n>.raw in --tmp-dir, the OS temp folder by default) before it renders; nothing is written until stdin reaches end of file; the spool holds the whole decoded input (frames x frame bytes) and is removed on every exit. Nothing appears on stdout while the decode runs.
suggested_handling: Pass --tmp-dir <run scratch folder>; check free space for frames x frame bytes (plus each layer) before starting; the encode only starts receiving data after the decode has finished, so progress and latency are those of two sequential phases; remove the scratch folder on error and interrupt.

what: A driver that writes all frames to vfx stdin before it reads stdout hangs (29 MB written, blocked after 8 s). A frame effect holds up to 1 MiB of output in its BufWriter, so the first output byte appeared (first bytes seen after 18 frames in (1105920 bytes); frames are 61440 bytes, the buffer is 1 MiB) and a write-one-read-one loop stalls. A reader thread fixes both.
suggested_handling: Three threads: decode to vfx stdin, vfx stdout to the encoder, vfx stderr drained. Never lock step. Temporal effects flush after every frame once rendering starts (src/temporal.rs render_all).

what: vfx exits 4 with 'input ends with a partial frame (N of M bytes) after K whole frames' when its input stops inside a frame. A frame effect has already written the K whole frames; a temporal effect measures the spool first and writes nothing. The crate never produces a partial frame itself (write_raw_frame and read_frame work in whole frames).
suggested_handling: Only reachable if the pipeline feeds a truncated buffer; keep frame sizes exact (PixFmt::frame_size) and report vfx's line.

area: short input on the encode side
what: ffmpeg exits 0 when the raw input stops inside a frame (5 whole frames plus 100 bytes: exit 0, 5 frames written, 'Invalid buffer size, packet size 100 < expected frame_size 61440' on stderr) and when the input is empty (exit 0). Encoder::finish() returns Ok with whatever was written. A vfx that died after N frames therefore leaves a short but valid output.
suggested_handling: Check the vfx exit status and the decode status as well as the encode's, compare frames written with the expected count, and run the apply.py style verification before moving the partial file.

area: damaged input on the decode side
what: ffmpeg exits 0 for a truncated Matroska file ('File ended prematurely', 62 of 120 frames) and for 200 corrupted bytes (decoder errors on stderr, 120 frames); the crate Decoder reports a clean end of stream. An mp4 without its moov atom exits non-zero (-1094995529 as i32) with no frame. Without --frames the output is simply shorter.
suggested_handling: Compare the number of decoded frames (or the duration) with the probe, as apply.py's verification does for the duration; treat a non empty Decoder::stderr() as a warning.

what: ffmpeg -n exits 0 when the output path exists ('File ... already exists. Exiting.') and writes nothing. Through the crate the first write then fails with Error::Io 'The pipe is being closed. (os error 232)' and no ffmpeg text; a short clip that fits in the pipe buffer would finish with Ok and an unchanged file.
suggested_handling: Remove any stale partial file first, as apply.py does, use a unique partial name (.partial-<pid>), and verify that the partial file exists and probes before moving it.

what: ffmpeg statuses are negated error codes. Rust reports them on Windows as negative i32 (-2, -542398533, -1094995529); Python reports 3199971767 for the same mp4 case. On a platform that keeps 8 bits a status is truncated.
suggested_handling: Print child statuses as numbers in messages and map all non zero statuses to the pipeline's single failure code.

what: vfx reads --fps 29.97 as the exact 2997/100, not 30000/1001; a constant speed gives the same output, but a keyframed ramp with a fractional key gave a different output (hash differs) from 30000/1001. A reducible fraction (60000/2002) gave the same output as 30000/1001. Decoder::fps and Encoder::fps take u32 numerator and denominator; ffprobe rationals are i64.
suggested_handling: Always hand vfx and ffmpeg the fraction from ffprobe (r_frame_rate or avg_frame_rate as N/D), never a float; refuse a rate whose parts do not fit u32 or whose denominator is 0.

what: The lossy path cannot encode an odd side: libx264 stops with 'width not divisible by 2 (161x97)' and the error reaches the crate at the first write after ffmpeg exits (after 5 frames in the run), as Error::Ffmpeg with exit code -542398533. The lossless ffv1 path takes odd sizes. Decoding to rgba of an odd size is fine.
suggested_handling: Refuse before decoding with apply.py's text (the frame size WxH has an odd side, and yuv420p needs even sides ...), unless lossless.

what: ffmpeg rotates frames by the display matrix, so the decoded size is the displayed size (96x160 for a 160x96 stream with rotation 90). The crate probe returns the coded size (160x96); the Decoder dry run measures the displayed size, an explicit size() with the coded size would distort.
suggested_handling: Swap width and height for rotation 90 or 270 (side_data_list rotation or the rotate tag) in the plan, as display_size does in apply.py.

what: apply.py maps the absolute stream index of the first video stream that is not attached_pic (-map 0:IDX). The crate maps the position among video streams (-map 0:v:N), and its default N=0 selects a leading still picture. The two are equal when N is counted correctly.
suggested_handling: Compute N as the number of video streams before IDX (needs the disposition field, R07). A leading attached picture is rare: the mp4 muxer writes it last.

what: The crate Decoder adds -fps_mode passthrough (and needs ffmpeg 5.1 or newer; timing_passthrough(false) removes it). apply.py does not. Bytes were identical with the fps filter (variable rate) and for constant rate inputs; without the fps filter the frame count of a variable rate input differs (R05).
suggested_handling: Keep the default; document the extra argument when printing the command lines (the dry run of the pipeline will differ from apply.py's text here).

what: A frame shown unchanged (retime at 100 percent) is bit exact for opaque frames at 8 and 32 bpc, differs by 1 in 174659 of 737280 samples at 16 bpc, and loses colour under alpha below 255 at 8 bpc (largest colour difference 13 at alpha 10, 255 at alpha 0, 1 at alpha 128); alpha itself is unchanged. This is the note of the twixtor README, measured again on this machine.
suggested_handling: Parity tests of an identity pipeline compare opaque 8 and 32 bpc bit for bit and 16 bpc within 1; a test with alpha below 255 compares alpha only.

what: ffmpeg's rgba to gbrapf32le conversion is not exactly value/255: up to 0.24 of one 8 bit step off for the values tried. Both the wrapper and the crate use the same ffmpeg, so decoded frames agree; an independent computation of value/255 would not.
suggested_handling: Compare against ffmpeg-decoded frames, not against arithmetic on the source samples.

what: When the reader of vfx stdout goes away, vfx exits 4 with 'write error: The pipe has been ended. (os error 109)' and the process feeding stdin gets a broken pipe (Python Errno 32). Rust writing to the stdin of an ffmpeg that has exited gets os error 232 'The pipe is being closed' (measured on ffmpeg, not on vfx).
suggested_handling: Treat BrokenPipe on the vfx stdin as 'vfx has ended' and report vfx's exit status and stderr line, not the pipe error.

what: vfx writes at most one line on stderr and ffmpeg a few lines at -loglevel error, but an undrained stderr pipe can block a child. The crate drains its own children (src/process.rs) and keeps 8 KiB of head and 56 KiB of tail; vfx is not one of them.
suggested_handling: Drain vfx stderr on a thread, or redirect it to a file in the scratch folder like apply.py.

what: Decoder::read_frame allocates a new Vec per frame; at 1080p and 32 bpc a frame is 33177600 bytes. read_frame_into reuses one buffer.
suggested_handling: Use read_frame_into with one buffer per stage and a bounded channel between the threads.

what: Encoder::finish waits at most 10 minutes (finish_timeout) after the input is closed and then kills ffmpeg (Error::Timeout); Decoder reads have no timeout; probes and size dry runs have 60 s.
suggested_handling: Raise finish_timeout for very large frames or slow presets; add a stall watchdog in the pipeline if needed.

what: Layer decoding (apply.py build_layer_commands and decode_layers) is not covered by any measurement here.
suggested_handling: Either leave layers out of the pipeline's first version and say so, or measure the layer recipe like the main decode.

what: 16 bpc lossless is requested as rgba64le and stored by ffv1 as gbrap16le; 8 bpc as bgra. Both decode back to the exact bytes vfx wrote. Depth 32 has no lossless path (ffv1 has no float format).
suggested_handling: Refuse --lossless with depth 32 with apply.py's text; use the round trip as the frame equality test.

what: Two ffv1 Matroska files of the same frames differ in their header (60 of 231212 bytes, first at 220), so file hashes cannot be compared; decoded frames are equal.
suggested_handling: Compare framemd5 or decoded raw frames.

what: vfx list --json hides the selftest effects; apply.py asks for --all first and falls back to the plain listing.
suggested_handling: Use --all when the effect id may be a selftest effect.

what: vfx apply --check validates ids, values and rates but not the refusals of a render (for example a foreground matte layer): the failure comes at frame 0 after the whole decode was spooled, exit 3, nothing written.
suggested_handling: Accept the wasted decode; report vfx's line; there is no cheaper pre-check.

what: Since 2026-10-26 19:17 tools/apply.py runs extra stages (--pre-stage, --post-stage). A stage is killed when no byte moves on either of its pipes for --stage-timeout seconds (default 120) while it is not waiting for a neighbour: a stage that reads its whole input and then computes silently for longer (the way vfx spools a temporal effect) is judged stalled. A stage that writes too many frames is not flagged by the stage checks; the run fails at verification. {frames} cannot be used with variable rate input.
suggested_handling: A sapphire stage should stream (read a frame, write a frame) and keep to the same frame count; if it must buffer, document --stage-timeout 0 or a larger value for it.

what: twixtor changed during the work: apply.py (stage slot, frames/1 error codes) and a handoff packet tool (tools/handoff.py, contracts/handoff-packet.schema.json, statuses new, accepted, done, failed, verified) appeared at 2026-10-26 19:17. contract.tsv rows are unaffected (decode, effect and encode argument lists and vfx.exe are unchanged), but any document about the wrapper must be checked against the new apply.py.
suggested_handling: Re-run scripts/verify.py stages and scripts/make_contract.py after any change in twixtor; the reviewer should read the current apply.py.
